title: Peak window backfill & headroom forecast Q4 2026
content:
Executive summary:

This working sheet captures an alternative framing for Q4 2026 hosted API peak-window planning focused on concentrated weekend and evening burst patterns and a backfill strategy to recover tail latency while preserving cost-efficiency. It defines region-by-region headroom targets expressed as tokens/sec and QPS and converts those targets to a minimal GPU-slice safety stock for fast procurement and autoscale policy tuning.

Key conclusions (working):
- Target global peak headroom: 28% above modeled 99th-percentile demand for conservative SLA posture during Q4 promo weeks.
- Prioritize compute headroom in NA-west and EU-central for weekend-evening windows; APAC gets smaller but faster spin-up pools.
- Backfill window strategy: allow 10-minute elastic backfill using burst-capable L4/H100 spare slices before moving to region-to-region overflow routing.

Assumptions and inputs (sources and notes):
- Baseline workload modeled from last 12 weeks of real traffic: median daily tokens/sec baseload ~220k global; 99th-percentile hourly peaks used to project growth and promotional multipliers.
- Q4 promotion multiplier scenarios: normal (x1.15), aggressive (x1.45), blackout (x2.0) for extreme flash sales.
- Average tokens per request assumed 325 tokens; average QPS = tokens/sec / avg_tokens_per_req.
- GPU performance: H100 (float16 optimized) baseline throughput ~120k tokens/sec per device for our long-chat mix; A100 80GB ~85k tps; L4 ~28k tps (cheap short-turn workloads).

Regional projection summary (peak tokens/sec target, 99th pct demand, headroom target):
- NA-west: modeled 99th = 360,000 t/s -> target headroom = 460,800 t/s (28% headroom) -> effective QPS = 1,418 QPS (avg 325 tokens).
- EU-central: modeled 99th = 240,000 t/s -> target = 307,200 t/s -> QPS = 945 QPS.
- APAC: modeled 99th = 90,000 t/s -> target = 115,200 t/s -> QPS = 354 QPS.
- Global aggregated target = 883,200 t/s (sum) -> global QPS = 2,717 QPS.

GPU-slice safety stock mapping (rounded up to nearest quarter-slice where slices are 1/8th device equivalent):
- NA-west: with H100 throughput 120k t/s -> nominal devices needed = 3.84 -> provision 5 devices (or 40 quarter-slices) to cover headroom + spare for maintenance.
- EU-central: A100-focused pools for cost control -> nominal devices = 3.62 (85k t/s) -> provision 5 devices.
- APAC: mix of L4 for fast spin-up + 1 H100 for heavy tails -> nominal combined devices equivalent ~2.1 -> provision 3 devices.

Scenarios (what to do per severity):
1) Normal weekend spike (x1.15): let autoscale handle ephemeral demand; pre-warm 20% of scheduled spare slices at T-30m for predicted high windows; monitor queue depth.
2) Aggressive promo (x1.45): trigger pre-provision plan at T-2h: increase dedicated pool by adding reserved slices and enable cross-region overflow routing to EU/NA depending on where latency impact is minimal.
3) Blackout/Flash (x2.0): invoke emergency surge runbook: shed best-effort low-priority traffic (embeds, offline bulk jobs), route to fallback model variants (quantized L4) and notify SRE/infra leads.

Backfill mechanics and constraints:
- Backfill window definition: 10 minutes of short-term excess capacity used to reduce request queue without increasing provisioned reserved commit. Backfill uses a high-priority queue and preemptible spot-like slices.
- Constraint: we observe latency amplification when concurrent KV cache warmups exceed 15% of device memory bandwidth; therefore staggered backfill (2-phase) is recommended: 0-5m aggressive short requests, 5-10m mixed longer contexts.

Operational runbook (short):
- T-60m: kick off capacity prediction check and post alert if predicted > 85% of headroom.
- T-30m: pre-warm N L4 slices per region (NA: 8, EU: 6, APAC: 3).
- T-10m: lock routing policy, raise max allowed batch size for H100 pools to improve throughput for long-chats.
- Spike detected above threshold: if sustained > 3m, auto-provision additional H100 quarter-slices from burst pool; otherwise, engage overflow.

Monitoring and metrics to add to Console dashboards (proposed):
- tokens_per_sec_99p_estimate (per-region, rolling 30m)
- headroom_pct (current provisioned / target - 1)
- queue_depth_by_priority (high/normal/low)
- cache_warmup_bandwidth_pct (per-device class)

Open questions / action items (owners):
- Validate H100 per-device token/sec using latest quantized kernels on test-deck (Arjun Patel) - due 2026-10-08.
- Confirm procurement lead time for 20 extra quarter-slices (Erika Summers) - due 2026-10-20.
- Add a simulation run for the aggressive promo (x1.45) using real promo traffic patterns (Maya Chen) - due 2026-10-06.

Appendix: short worked example
- If NA-west observed 420k t/s sustained for 7 minutes and our queued average tokens/request is 300, then QPS demand = 1,400. With our headroom target (28%), we need 1,792 QPS capacity -> with H100 throughput that maps to ~4 devices; if pool already at 4 devices, trigger backfill + overflow.

Notes: this is a working forecast; it intentionally uses conservative headroom for Q4 promo weeks. Comments welcome inline.
